title: Add compatibility tags and pricing hints to model listing endpoints
author: Marina Chen
commits_summary: 4 commits: initial API and DB migration; SDK deserialization + docs; backfill script and cache/index optimizations; tests and CI fixes
description:
Motivation: teams building against the model listing endpoint need richer, first-class capability signals and lightweight pricing/limit hints so routing, UI filters, and compatibility shims can make informed choices without heavy probing. This PR introduces an opt-in enrichment for the model catalog API that surfaces capability tags and simple pricing/limit hints while remaining backward-compatible with existing clients.

What this changes (summary):
- API: /v1/models listing and single-model detail now include a capability_metadata object with canonical tags and hints. New top-level fields returned in JSON for each model: "capability_tags" (array of short strings), "pricing_hint" (object with cost_per_token_usd and recommended_batch_size), and "limits_hint" (object with max_sequence_length and recommended_max_output_tokens). The list response supports a new query param filter 'capabilities' (comma-separated) and 'max_cost' for lightweight server-side filtering.
- Compatibility flags: adds explicit tags such as streaming, function_calling, structured_output, openai_compat, kv_cache_friendly, and quantized_profiles:<profile-name>. The openai_compat tag is intended to signal mapping fidelity to OpenAI-style semantics (where applicable).
- DB: added new JSONB column capability_metadata to model_catalog, plus an indexed derived column capability_tags (text[]) to accelerate capability filters. Included migrations and a backfill script that populates capability_metadata from existing model records and onboarding scripts.
- SDKs: Python and TypeScript SDKs updated to deserialize capability_tags/pricing_hint/limits_hint and expose helpers for filtering locally when necessary.
- Tools & docs: model-inspector CLI prints capability hints; docs updated with examples for filtering and for how to interpret pricing_hint.
- Tests: added unit tests for deserialization, integration tests for the new query params, and a small end-to-end that validates filter behavior against the test catalog.

Backward compatibility and rollout:
- The new fields are additive; old clients ignore them. The listing filter 'capabilities' will only be enabled when the feature flag 'model_catalog_enrichment' is present on the tenant. Default behavior for tenants without the flag remains unchanged. We will roll the FF to 50% of tenants for 48 hours, monitor error/hit rates, then 100%.

Performance considerations & mitigation:
- To avoid full table scans on capability filters we added a GIN index on capability_tags and maintain a small materialized text[] column updated on writes.
- Backfill script is throttled and uses pagination; a separate admin job can be triggered for large catalogs.
- Catalog cache TTL shortened temporarily after rollout to ensure stale entries with missing capability metadata are refreshed quickly.

CI / Review notes: initial CI run failed due to a TS lint rule in sdk/ts after I renamed a helper; fix committed in second commit. Integration tests initially flagged an edge case where unknown capability strings caused a crash in the old deserializer — added safe-guarding to ignore unknown tags and map to "unknown".

Review conversation (excerpt):
- Aisha: "We should gate the filter so large customers don't see behavior changes unexpectedly. Also recommend an event in audit logs when capability metadata is backfilled."
  Marina: "Agreed. Feature flag gate added and backfill writes an audit event per model. See scripts/backfill_capabilities.py commit."
- Miguel: "Can we expose a simple enum for openai_compat levels (partial/full/none) instead of a boolean?"
  Marina: "We kept a short string tag for now (openai_compat:partial|full) to avoid changing the proto shape; SDK helpers will surface an enum wrapper for convenience. Added tests for both values."
- Lin: "Docs need to show how pricing_hint should be interpreted (approximate only)."
  Marina: "Docs updated with examples and a note that pricing_hint is advisory only and may be conservative."

Merge and post-merge actions:
- After approvals and CI green, this was squash-merged to main. Post-merge: scheduled DB migration for next maintenance window (included in this PR but gated by ops schedule), and feature flag rollout plan recorded in ENG-4211.

Related work: ENG-4211 (model routing and catalog enrichment), PM-998 (product requirements for compatibility filters).

Notes for SDKs and integrators:
- Python: new Model.capability_tags (list[str]), Model.pricing_hint (dict), Model.limits_hint (dict). Helper redwood.models.get_openai_compat_level() returns "none|partial|full".
- TS: models.ts adds typed interfaces and a filter helper models.filterByCapabilities(models, ["streaming"]).

This PR aims to provide a stable, discoverable surface for capability-driven routing and UI filters without forcing immediate behavior changes for existing users. The enrichment is behind a feature flag and includes migration tooling and tests to minimize risk.
release_notes:
- Add capability tags (streaming, function_calling, structured_output, openai_compat, etc.) to model listing and detail endpoints.
- Introduce pricing_hint and limits_hint fields to help routing/UI with lightweight cost/limit signals.
- Add 'capabilities' filter for server-side model listing.
- DB migrations and backfill tooling included.
- SDK updates (Python/TS) to surface new fields.
notes_for_ops: Run db/migrations/20260218_add_model_capability_metadata.sql during maintenance window. Trigger scripts/backfill_capabilities.py with --throttle before enabling feature flag for large tenants.
risk_summary: Low-medium: additive API fields only. Main risk is DB backfill and index churn; mitigations included (throttled backfill, gated FF, cache TTL adjustments).
